questions.promptVi: [Đọc hiểu đoạn văn] Đọc đoạn hội thoại sau và trả lời câu hỏi:
questions.passage:
Coach Oliver: "Welcome to our intensive pronunciation clinic! Today, we master the three distinct sounds of regular '-ed' endings."
Jessica: "Many students get confused when reading past tense verbs aloud. Can you guide us through the rules?"
Coach Oliver: "Certainly! Rule one: When a verb ends with the sound /t/ or /d/, '-ed' is pronounced as an extra syllable: /ɪd/."
Jessica: "For instance: 'wanted' /wɒntɪd/, 'needed' /niːdɪd/, 'decided' /dɪˈsaɪdɪd/, and 'invited' /ɪnˈvaɪtɪd/!"

Lịch trình đi du lịch nghỉ mát cuối tuần

questions.promptVi: [Đọc hiểu đoạn văn] Đọc đoạn đối thoại tiếp theo và chọn nhận định đúng:
questions.passage:
Coach Oliver: "Spot on! Rule two: After voiceless consonant sounds like /p, k, f, s, ʃ, tʃ/, '-ed' is pronounced as a crisp /t/."
Jessica: "Like 'walked' /wɔːkt/, 'watched' /wɒtʃt/, 'laughed' /lɑːft/, and 'kissed' /kɪst/!"
Coach Oliver: "Rule three: After all other voiced sounds and vowels, '-ed' smoothly vibrates as /d/."
Jessica: "Examples include 'played' /pleɪd/, 'cleaned' /kliːnd/, 'lived' /lɪvd/, and 'opened' /əʊpənd/."
